title: Finite compact Hausdorff affine charts for quasi-compact schemes with closed points
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] that is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and suppose every singleton in its underlying topological space is closed. Then there exist a finite set $I$, affine open subschemes $U_i\subseteq X$, commutative rings $A_i$, and isomorphisms $U_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], for $i\in I$, such that $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, every prime ideal of every $A_i$ is maximal, and each $U_i$ in its subspace topology is quasi-compact and Hausdorff. Here Hausdorff means that any two distinct points admit disjoint open neighbourhoods. The set $I$ may be empty when $X=\varnothing$. No quasi-separatedness, Noetherianity or finite-type assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover] to the quasi-compact scheme $X$. Obtain a finite affine open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$. By the definition of affine in [def-pc-scheme], choose a commutative ring $A_i$ and a scheme isomorphism $h_i:U_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for each $i$. If $X=\varnothing$, take $I=\varnothing$ and all remaining assertions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens, followed by quasi-compactness; Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, finite affine covering in the final paragraph

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$. Every singleton $\{u\}\subset U_i$ is closed in $U_i$, because it is the intersection of the closed singleton $\{u\}\subset X$ with $U_i$, with its subspace topology. The underlying map of the scheme isomorphism $h_i$ is a homeomorphism, so every singleton in $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is closed as well.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, opening paragraph: closed-point formulation of dimension zero on each affine chart

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p$ be any prime of $A_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], $V(\mathfrak p)=\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}=\{\mathfrak p\}$, where the last equality uses step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$. A maximal ideal of a commutative ring is prime: if $ab\in\mathfrak m$ and $a\notin\mathfrak m$, write $1=c+ra$ with $c\in\mathfrak m$ and multiply by $b$ to obtain $b\in\mathfrak m$. Hence $\mathfrak m\in V(\mathfrak p)=\{\mathfrak p\}$, so $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$ is maximal.

source.place: Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible, (1); Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, (2) and (8); maximal-prime criterion in Tag 04MG, lemma-ring-with-only-minimal-primes

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-spectrum-profinite] to $A_i$, whose every prime is maximal by step 3. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is compact Hausdorff. Pulling an open cover of $U_i$ across the homeomorphism $h_i$ and pulling a finite subcover back proves quasi-compactness of $U_i$; pulling back disjoint open neighbourhoods proves Hausdorffness of $U_i$. The finite family from step 1 now has every property required. No property of intersections of charts was used.
